# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running

## Quick picks

| Pick | Price seen | Battery (buds) | Water rating | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | $199 (list $299) | ~7–7.5 h | IPX4 | Best sound and stability |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | $125–$180 | 12 h | IP55 | Hearing traffic best |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | $200 | 10 h (40 with case) | IP57 | Long runs and rain |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** | $99 (list $149) | Long | IP54 | Mid-price value |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | ~$80–$104 | 10 h (42 with case) | IP55 | Budget |
| **JLab Flex Open** | ~$40 | 7 h | IP55 per JLab | Trying open-ear cheaply |

## Details

**1. Bose Ultra Open Earbuds: best overall**
- Runner's World ranks it #1 after 2,200+ logged miles. It doesn't bounce, works with hats and glasses, and leaks less sound than most.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-stride than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 only, so skip it if you run in heavy rain often. Battery is about 7 hours.
- Timing: as of late September, Runner's World said Bose would release new open earbuds "within the next month." Check whether they've launched before buying.
- It's $199 at Bose and Best Buy. [WIRED guide with buy links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) · [Runner's World review](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**2. Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: best for road safety**
- Bone conduction keeps your ears fully open, so you hear traffic best.
- It has physical buttons, USB-C charging and 12-hour battery life. WIRED rates it 8/10.
- Downsides: the neckband can clash with ponytails, hoods and high collars. Bass is better than older Shokz models but still thinner than the Bose.
- It's $125 at REI and Best Buy, versus $180 at Amazon. [WIRED review with buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS: Bose vs. Shokz](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**3. Shokz OpenDots 2: best for marathon training and wet weather**
- WIRED's overall #1. It has 10 hours of battery and an IP57 rating, and WIRED's tester has submerged it without problems.
- It costs $200 at Amazon, Best Buy and Shokz. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**4. Nothing Ear (Open): strong value**
- SoundGuys picks it as best for running. It has the best bass in its lab tests, a full EQ and IP54.
- It's $99 at Amazon. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**5. Soundcore AeroFit 2: budget pick**
- SoundGuys' best budget pick. It has an adjustable ear hook, IP55, 10 hours of battery and LDAC on Android.
- Price check: there are two prices out there.
  - Dealectric lists **$104** at Soundcore's store with code **AFSC20**. That listing was cart-tested on Oct 22, the code expires 12/31, and the link is an affiliate link. [Buy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2)
  - SoundGuys showed it at **$79.99 on Amazon**, but that price is from January 2026.
  - Check Amazon before using the code. If Amazon is still under $104, buy there.

**6. JLab Flex Open: cheapest way to try open-ear**
- About $40 at Amazon and Walmart. The sound is weaker, but it stays put. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Which to choose
- **Running on busy roads:** OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound in a clip-on, mostly dry weather:** Bose Ultra Open, but check for the new model first.
- **Long runs or rain:** OpenDots 2.
- **Under $100:** Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

If you tell me your budget, whether you use iPhone or Android, and whether you wear glasses or hats, I can narrow this down.
